expectations.text: Correctly states this is a proposed rule (NPRM, published January 2025) that would remove 'addressable' designations and mandate MFA/encryption — it is NOT final and NOT in effect
expectations.evidence: "OCR published a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRM) in early January 2025... eliminate the long-standing distinction between 'required' and 'addressable'... a proposed rule is not law... no new enforceable MFA/encryption mandate in effect"

expectations.text: States the current status: the August 2026 Unified Agenda moved the rule to Long-Term Actions with final action anticipated around July 2027
expectations.evidence: No mention of the August 2026 Unified Agenda, Long-Term Actions, or July 2027 timing; only "As of now, no final rule has been published"

expectations.text: States that the existing Security Rule (with required vs addressable implementation specifications) remains the operative law to comply with today
expectations.evidence: "The current Security Rule (45 CFR §164.312) already lists encryption... as an 'addressable' implementation specification... Addressable does not mean optional" — current rule presented as operative law

expectations.text: Mentions the industry pushback: 100+ hospital systems / provider associations (AHA-led) have urged HHS to withdraw or substantially revise the proposal
expectations.evidence: No mention of AHA-led industry pushback or 100+ hospital systems urging withdrawal; response even says rulemaking "rarely gets weaker between proposal and final rule"

expectations.text: Gives the right advice: build against the current Security Rule now, track the proposal, and do not treat NPRM provisions as current legal requirements — while noting MFA/encryption are best practice regardless
expectations.evidence: "don't tell stakeholders you are legally required to comply with the NPRM today — you're not... start or continue a project to implement encryption... and MFA... good security hygiene regardless; monitor the Federal Register"
